name: Neo-Confucianism
summary: Neo-Confucianism is the Song-Ming revival of Confucian thought, systematised by Zhu Xi, which grounds ethics in a rational cosmic principle (li) and holds that people are originally good and can become sages through study and self-cultivation. Its politics are moral and hierarchical: rulers should govern by virtue and example, officials should be chosen by learning, and order rests on ritual, filial piety and the family, with local voluntary institutions of education and relief preferred to court centralization. It treats profit-seeking and selfishness as the root of disorder and accepts removal of a tyrant only as an extraordinary exception.
scope: The Cheng-Zhu school (Cheng Yi, Cheng Hao, Zhu Xi) as the state-orthodox Neo-Confucianism of the Song through Qing dynasties, drawing on the Four Books and Zhu Xi's Family Rituals; Wang Yangming's mind-school is used only where it does not diverge. It is a moral philosophy with political implications, not a modern political programme, so most modern policy statements are low-confidence inferences from its principles; Korean, Japanese and Vietnamese variants and modern New Confucianism are not the basis.

keyFigures.name: Zhu Xi
keyFigures.role: Systematiser of the Cheng-Zhu school and compiler of the Four Books as the examination core

keyFigures.name: Wang Yangming
keyFigures.role: Leading critic of Zhu Xi who founded the mind-school (xinxue)

keyFigures.name: Cheng Yi
keyFigures.role: Northern Song philosopher whose teaching with his brother Cheng Hao Zhu Xi built on

sources.title: Zhu Xi
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Zhu Xi's career: criticism of corrupt officials, academies, Four Books in examinations, persecution.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a Song-Ming question; Zhu Xi's relief granaries and benevolent government suggest care for the needy, but sources do not discuss health provision, so split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage-setting is not addressed; the Great Learning's stress on not squeezing the people points toward humane rule but gives no view on a legal wage floor.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Great Learning says wealth is the result of virtue and warns rulers against making revenue their chief business, so unregulated markets as better allocators is inferred as disfavoured.

public-ownership.rationale: Neo-Confucians favoured local autonomy and voluntary community bodies over central state control, so national public ownership of industries is inferred as unfavoured.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Great Learning opposes heavy imposts on the people but also condemns wealth gained unrighteously; no stated view on progressive taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Guilds and unions as such are not discussed; voluntary community organisations were favoured, but nothing specific about labor unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private property was assumed in gentry society, but Neo-Confucians also proposed land equalization, so a near-absolute right is not stated.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations did not exist; the moral critique of profit-seeking implies some sympathy but no regulatory programme is documented.

cut-welfare.rationale: Zhu Xi promoted relief and benevolent local provision, so cutting welfare as dependency-creating is inferred as opposed; the sources say little directly.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; Neo-Confucian economic thought centred on peasant households and gentry, not worker-owned firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not discussed; order and moral cultivation are valued but sources give no view on counter-terror surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Self-cultivation and restraint of excess desire are central, so recreational drug legalisation is inferred as disfavoured, though the sources never discuss drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; adherents valued harmony and moral speech but no law-based speech regulation is documented.

strong-leader.rationale: Zhu Xi proposed a committee of upright experts to review imperial decisions as a check on arbitrary rule, and Neo-Confucians opposed court centralization.

state-harmful.rationale: Neo-Confucians held that ethical norms should govern political and social life through ritual and ruler, so a stateless view is flatly contrary to the tradition.

limit-guns.rationale: Not discussed; a rule-by-virtue approach has no stated stance on firearms.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Great Learning prefers moral example to force and Confucian officials ranked civil above military power; more coercive authority is inferred as disfavoured.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sexual propriety and ritual norms in family life were central, so legalising sex work is inferred as disfavoured; no direct source.

decide-locally.rationale: Neo-Confucians opposed centralization at the imperial court and favoured local autonomy and voluntary local organizations.

rehabilitation.rationale: Moral transformation of persons through education is central, and Zhu Xi held anyone can progress toward sagehood, so reform over punishment fits.

traditional-family.rationale: Zhu Xi's Family Rituals and his stress on filial piety and respect for elder brothers make the ritual-ordered family the foundation of society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Marriage ritual was centred on continuing the patriline through Family Rituals; not discussed directly, inferred as opposed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Family continuity and the value of life are stressed but abortion is not discussed in the sources; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Confucianism's religious status is debated by scholars and Neo-Confucians criticized Buddhism, so a larger public role for religion is split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; Neo-Confucianism has no framework of racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Distinct roles were grounded in cosmic principle li and yin-yang order, so gender as mainly social construction is inferred as rejected.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Zhu Xi aimed to restore China's Confucian cultural identity against non-Chinese challenges, and reviving classical culture was the movement's aim.

gradual-change.rationale: Neo-Confucians stressed moral cultivation and ritual continuity, with reform via education and local institutions rather than overturning institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; the culturalist rather than racial view of Chinese identity gives no clear answer.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Anachronistic; the tradition centred on a Sinocentric order, so supranational power is inferred as unfavoured.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition's moral critique of profit-seeking does not yield a stated trade policy.

nation-first.rationale: Zhu Xi's concern was cultural restoration against outsiders, but modern national-interest framing is anachronistic; split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; the ruler's moral example, not force, was the way to influence, so intervention is inferred as disfavoured.

open-borders.rationale: Cultural Chinese identity versus outsiders was a concern for Zhu Xi; open borders is inferred as disfavoured.

limit-growth.rationale: Heaven-earth-human harmony is a theme but economic growth limits are not discussed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; the triad of heaven, earth and humans suggests care for nature but no policy stance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Moral cultivation, not technique, is the solution to social problems for Neo-Confucians; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Zhu Xi countenanced removing an evil ruler only as an extraordinary case of discretion; reform through moral remonstrance was the norm, so revolution is not generally endorsed.

experts-over-public.rationale: Zhu Xi proposed a committee of morally upright experts to review imperial decisions, and learning-based official selection was central.

central-planning.rationale: Opposition to court centralization and favouring of local voluntary bodies lead to inference against central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Worker or public ownership of firms in a market is a modern design with no Neo-Confucian treatment, so the answer is neutral.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed in the sources used.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Lineage and inheritance via ancestral rites matter, but sources do not discuss inheritance tax.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; relief and benevolent provision for the needy is approved but unconditional income is not discussed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade protection is not discussed in the sources, and the tradition gives no principle that decides it.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Local autonomy and community-based initiative were preferred to centralized direction; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Agrarian peasant-household economy with concern against concentrated wealth appears in the tradition, though the sources used do not state it; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wealth as the result of virtue and hierarchical household order are assumed, and no Neo-Confucian source envisions abolishing money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Voluntary local organizations were favoured, but state-recognised wage bodies are not discussed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rule by a morally educated scholar-official class is approved, but party rule is anachronistic; Neo-Confucian scholars also stood apart from government.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Great Learning and the imperial context assume a ruler who governs by virtue as parent of the people; monarchy is accepted when the ruler is morally cultivated.

democracy-best.rationale: Government was by morally trained scholar-officials and a sage-ruler ideal; popular sovereignty was not endorsed, though the Great Learning says the kingdom is gained by gaining the people.

direct-votes.rationale: Moral and learned guidance of policy rather than mass votes fits the tradition; direct legislation by citizens is inferred as unfavoured.

workers-councils.rationale: Hierarchical scholar-led government, not class councils, is assumed.

right-to-secede.rationale: Zhu Xi sought cultural and political unity of the empire; right to secede inferred as opposed.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Great Learning holds that rulers must first possess good qualities themselves, and Neo-Confucianism pursued sagehood through self-cultivation, making moral and learned superiors the fit rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Zhu Xi allowed extraordinary removal of a tyrant, while the norm was peaceful remonstrance; adherents are split on an absolute rule.

war-builds-character.rationale: Moral example and benevolent rule, not martial valour, are praised in the Great Learning; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Confucianism's religious status is contested and no church exists; the concept scarcely applies.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Classics (Four Books) served as curriculum and moral basis, but law was not derived from scripture as in sharia; split.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state's ethical order and public-spirited gong against selfishness si make privatized courts and defense contrary to the tradition.

military-superiority.rationale: None of the opened sources states a doctrine of military primacy; Zhu Xi opposed appeasement but that is not a stance on superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Chinese identity was cultural, defined by Confucian civilization, not ethnicity; split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Social order and harmony based on principle in a ritual hierarchy is the ideal, contrary to class conflict as the motor of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy by moral and educational attainment is accepted, but ethical concern for the poor; equal outcomes is not sought.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The sources contain no discussion of indigenous land claims, and no principle of the school decides it.

civilizational-union.rationale: The Sinocentric civilizational order is part of the tradition's background, but modern political unions are not discussed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The tradition opposes si (selfishness) and partiality to gong (public spirit), so pursuing self-interest as morally good is rejected.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Li (ritual) as social glue and filial piety as primary relationship make duties to family and community come first; rights language is absent.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Heaven, earth and humans form an ordered triad, and the principle li is expressed in all things, implying value beyond utility.

limit-population.rationale: Lineage continuity and large families are valued; population limits are inferred as disfavoured.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anachronistic; the tradition assumes an ordered civilization and does not condemn it wholesale.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The tradition prizes ritual continuity and moral cultivation over disrupting institutions, so accelerating disruptive change is inferred as opposed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Perfecting oneself through moral cultivation rather than technology is the Neo-Confucian path; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Government by morally cultivated persons exercising discretion (quan) is central, so handing decisions to algorithms is contrary to the tradition.

restore-past-order.rationale: Zhu Xi sought to restore a Confucian cultural and political identity grounded in the ancient sage teachings, though moral progress toward sagehood is also central.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Chen Liang's pragmatism was never well received and Zhu Xi rejected it, preferring principle-based judgement over outcomes alone.

direct-action.rationale: Reform by education, remonstrance, and local institution-building rather than confrontation; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: The Great Learning ties order of the state to cultivation of the person, so means must embody the virtue sought.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The ritual-ordered civilization and learning are the basis of the tradition, so primitivism is contrary to it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Neo-Confucianism assumes distinct social roles, with scholars teaching and rulers governing.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed; benevolence to the needy but no distributive principle stated.

production-for-use.rationale: The critique of profit-seeking by rulers is there, but no stance on production for use.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Profit-making and exploitation as a class mechanism is foreign to the tradition, whose moral economy rests on virtue as root and wealth as result.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship contradicts rule by moral example and harmonious hierarchy.

collective-farming.rationale: Family-based agriculture and household filial order are assumed; collectivization inferred as opposed.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a Neo-Confucian analysis; war and disorder come from lack of rulers' virtue, so inferred as rejected.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Great Learning warns against excessive imposts but takes revenue for a ruler who serves the people as legitimate; taxation is not theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Ethical norms were meant to apply to all political and social life, so state limits are not confined to preventing harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Persons are defined through relationships and family and community duty; rights belonging only to individuals contradicts this.

conscription.rationale: Not discussed; civil primacy over military yet duty to state.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Remonstrance and the ruler's gaining of the people's heart are the checks, rather than exit; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: The Great Learning criticizes rulers who make revenue their chief business and says righteousness, not gain, is the state's benefit.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not framed in liberty terms; benevolent provision is valued.

media-academia-power.rationale: Scholars' moral authority outside government was valued, but the claim as stated is a modern one.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Zhu Xi held qi endowment shapes disposition but anyone can progress toward sagehood; race as destiny is not part of it.

organic-representation.rationale: Voluntary local community bodies and family-based order fit, though representation theory is not stated.

total-state.rationale: Neo-Confucians opposed centralization and favoured autonomous local and scholarly institutions outside government.

national-rebirth.rationale: Zhu Xi aimed at cultural renewal, but radical rebirth framing is not used.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Rule by virtue drawing others to it, not conquest, is the Confucian ideal; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Loyalty of minister to ruler is part of the five relationships, but lord-follower oaths are a different structure.

bound-labor.rationale: Not addressed; benevolent government and the parent-of-the-people ideal point against serfdom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Neo-Confucians held that reality is knowable through reason, with principle li discoverable by investigation of things.

universal-morality.rationale: Zhu Xi held that principle (li) expresses the Way of Heaven and can be known by investigating things, and human nature is originally good everywhere.

single-common-good.rationale: The contrast of gong (public-minded) with si (selfish) and partial interests makes the common good, found by moral reason, the aim of politics.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora citizenship rights are a modern question that Neo-Confucian sources never take up.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not discussed; classical Chinese was kept alive by examinations, which does not settle the modern question.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Hierarchical order by moral authority, not democratic firm governance, is assumed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Zhu Xi founded his own academy dissatisfied with local schools, but vouchers are not addressed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The Great Learning cautions against rulers' pursuit of revenue, but fiscal macro policy is not addressed.

economic-freedom.rationale: The sources do not link political and economic freedom; the school's moral critique of gain gives no clear answer.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Great Learning states that the ruler must himself possess the good qualities before requiring them of the people, and the Confucian rule by moral example underlies it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Anachronistic; only the general warning against rulers pursuing revenue as their chief business is relevant.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nation-state self-determination is a modern concept; Zhu Xi's cultural identity concern gives no clear answer.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Neo-Confucians stressed knowing principle by reasoned investigation of things, but also reverent mindfulness and meditation; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; community relief was local rather than defined by citizenship.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Moral self-effort and avoidance of dependence are valued alongside relief, so a work requirement is inferred as mildly favoured.

class-collaboration.rationale: Harmony of social roles and public-spirited gong over partiality favour cooperation of all in an ordered society over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Neo-Confucianism was itself a project of recovering and teaching the classical canon, with Zhu Xi compiling the Four Books, so sacrificing inherited culture for novelty is the opposite of its aim.

workers-nation.rationale: Whether workers organise nationally or internationally is a modern labour question absent from the tradition.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Zhu Xi's Family Rituals and the five relationships assign differentiated family roles, though he allowed discretion such as widow remarriage; public-role law is inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: The Great Learning's disdain for gain does not yield a documented ban on interest; split among adherents.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Chinese civilization was defined by cultural attainment and anyone can approach sagehood, so legal racial classification is contrary to it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is meant to be the moral parent of the people, per the Great Learning, not an instrument of one class.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Zhu Xi stressed Confucian cultural identity as the ideal for the empire, so adoption of the host culture is inferred as favoured.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no basis in the tradition's moral-rational framework, and Confucian thought treats culture as acquired by learning.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems were not part of the tradition.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading Confucian civilization by moral example is a theme, but the statement's political-form mission is not stated; split.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Neo-Confucians regarded hierarchical gender and family roles as principled order, not as a structure of systematic disadvantage, though women scholars debated emotion.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Zhu Xi was demoted for attacking incompetence and corruption of influential officials, and the tradition critiques officials who pursue gain.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Zhu Xi held that all can progress toward sagehood despite differing qi endowments, and family continuity was prized; eugenics not addressed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability of security forces for past abuses is not covered by the opened sources.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Ethical norms were to inform all political and social life and the state educates and relieves the people, so a minimal state is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Cultural rather than racial boundaries defined Chinese identity; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Zhu Xi taught that anyone who sincerely commits can move toward sagehood and human nature is originally good, but social roles and rank differ, so equal rights are not stated.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist debate with no counterpart in Neo-Confucian thought.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism is a modern analytic category that the sources do not touch.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; ritual law varied by role and family.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Neo-Confucians criticized Buddhism but sources do not state legal restrictions; split.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle slaughter has no place in the opened sources and no stated principle of the school applies.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The state curriculum was itself the moral-philosophical Four Books, so excluding moral-religious teaching is inferred as disfavoured.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Soviet doctrine with no counterpart in the sources on Neo-Confucianism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Great Learning says the kingdom is gained or lost by gaining the people, a moral not procedural basis; formal consent is not stated, so split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export surplus as an aim is mercantilist policy that the sources do not discuss.

population-transfer.rationale: Benevolent rule and moral example as the way to bring in outsiders; transfers inferred as disfavoured.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Moral example over force is preferred, but Zhu Xi allowed removing a tyrant; so only mildly favours.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Harmony and moral cultivation, not struggle, are the stated engine of improvement; selfish competition is condemned as si.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party outlawing is not covered, as the tradition had no parties in the modern sense.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not framed in these terms, though the check on arbitrary imperial rule via a committee of upright experts is relevant.

separated-powers.rationale: Zhu Xi's proposed expert committee to review imperial decisions shows sympathy with a check on arbitrary power, but not a doctrine of separation.

vanguard-party.rationale: The tradition holds that moral teaching can be provided by scholars outside government for all, not a disciplined vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Benevolent government and community relief were Neo-Confucian projects, but priority to the poor is not stated as doctrine.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are a modern British policy question outside the tradition.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Social harmony and order are valued over confrontation; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The opened sources do not give the school's causal view of poverty and population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cohesion was sought through shared ritual and culture; ethnic diversity itself not discussed.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Office through learning and moral worth, with Zhu Xi's Four Books in examinations, is the opposite of random selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Zhu Xi allowed discretion (quan) in extraordinary cases, but emergency powers are not addressed.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Relief granaries are known for Zhu Xi but the sources I opened do not describe price policy.

party-controls-media.rationale: Neo-Confucians favoured teaching by scholars outside government, which implies no state control of information.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party concepts are anachronistic; civil control of arms by the ruler was assumed.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not addressed in the opened sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; officials' frugality was valued.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Zhu Xi was a critic of political factions; inferred as disfavouring binding party discipline.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The emperor commanded the forces in the system the tradition worked within; not argued.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by scholar-officials trained in the classics is favoured, not by priests, though they resemble a learned authority; contested.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Loyalty and remonstrance and Zhu Xi's concern for the empire against outsiders make working for defeat of one's own government contrary.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The tradition links moral character to rule and culture, but Zhu Xi's own stance on censorship is not in the sources; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term limits are a modern constitutional matter not found in the sources.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed; officials were subject to imperial review and remonstrance.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Permanent military alliances are not discussed; the school's foreign-policy concern was cultural defence against outsiders.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from acceptance of ordinary property arrangements.

people-in-arms.rationale: Civil scholar-led order was preferred to militias; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Local rural community organization and agrarian morality figured in Neo-Confucian reform, but not a stated claim.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Zhu Xi's father left office over opposing appeasement of the Jurchen, and Zhu sought the empire's cultural and political unity.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The tradition's ideal ruler and official is the educated moral person, and Zhu Xi held learning as the path to sagehood.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Zhu Xi held Confucian ethics necessary for China against non-Chinese challenges, treating that civilization as normatively higher.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, but classical punishment of grave crimes was accepted; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum was the Four Books and ritual; sex education and gender equality teaching inferred as disfavoured.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Neo-Confucian cosmology was rational-naturalist, through li and qi, not a creator-god; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Ritual propriety and moral restraint of excessive emotion without principle are central; restriction is inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Cultural membership, not descent, defined Chinese identity, but lineage is prized; split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Minority-language policy is not covered in the sources I opened.

religious-exemptions.rationale: A single ritual-moral order was assumed; exemptions inferred as disfavoured.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Li as social glue and cultivation under norms mean conformity to ritual is a good, not a harm.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt relief is a modern issue the sources do not address.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: This anti-colonial claim has no counterpart in the sources on Neo-Confucianism.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making by an elected assembly is unrelated to the tradition; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Developmentalist trade-offs between freedom and growth are not covered by the opened sources.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Great Learning's benevolence and Zhu Xi's love extending beyond the family to all things suggest duty to aid, but international framing is anachronistic.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic here and no principle of the school decides the question.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state in the tradition is the moral ruler who governs by example; popular election is not part of it.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is anachronistic for the tradition, so no position can be drawn from the sources.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Zhu Xi's father opposed appeasement of the Jurchen, but modern land-for-peace deals are not addressed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Gong over si and the Great Learning's wealth-follows-virtue suggest property is subordinate to moral ends, though not stated as doctrine.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The character of the Soviet economy is a Marxist dispute that the tradition's sources never address.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is anachronistic and the opened sources give no principle for it.

collective-defense.rationale: Mutual-defence treaties are not covered in the opened sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The legal status of annexed territory is a modern international-law question not found in the sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: No church; scholars taught outside government and Neo-Confucians criticized Buddhism, so split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The ruler as parent of the people who loves what they love fits a head of state above factions, though not a stated doctrine.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Unity of the empire was assumed by Zhu Xi; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Local autonomy favoured, but special arrangements for regions are not discussed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The ruler is morally accountable to Heaven and could be removed in extremity, per Zhu Xi's discussion, so divine descent as such is not a Neo-Confucian claim.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not covered; the Great Learning only warns against excessive levies on the people.

character-from-environment.rationale: Zhu Xi said qi endowment, family and environment shape dispositions, while nature is originally good; adherents hold both, so split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The ruler is bound by moral principle and Zhu Xi proposed expert review of imperial decisions to check arbitrary rule.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is anachronistic and the sources give no relevant principle.

leader-cult.rationale: The Great Learning's rule by moral example does not entail mass personality worship; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not discussed; Family Rituals concern ritual roles, not modern custody presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not applicable and class struggle is contrary to the tradition's harmony.

land-redistribution.rationale: Neo-Confucians such as Zhu Xi discussed land equalization but the sources I opened do not describe it; split.

refugee-return.rationale: The return of refugees is a modern question not covered in the opened sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Cultural and not ethnic identity defines the community; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Neo-Confucians criticized Buddhism intellectually but no legal punishment for leaving a religion is recorded in the sources.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is anachronistic and not covered by the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Union of peoples by language family is not part of the Neo-Confucian civilizational model, and the sources do not address it.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Local autonomy supported but not for national minorities as such.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Diaspora strategy for minorities is not discussed in the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Moral cultivation and principle li drive social order, not material production; Neo-Confucian idealism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not covered; the tradition's critique of gain gives no clear rule on cartels.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm bailouts are modern fiscal questions not covered by the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Judicial review of majority decisions is a modern constitutional matter outside the tradition's sources.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Differentiated roles inferred; quotas for public bodies unfavoured.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Imperial economic blocs are not discussed in the opened sources on the school.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Standards in trade agreements are modern and not addressed by the sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Great Learning puts virtue as the root and wealth the result, and rulers should lead by moral example rather than material gain.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Violent seizure of power conflicts with the norm of remonstrance and moral example; removal of a tyrant is only an extraordinary exception.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hierarchy by moral and learned attainment, with civil service exam based selection, undercuts but did not abolish hereditary status; family lineage rites persisted.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Zhu Xi sought to restore China's Confucian cultural identity and teach the Four Books; civilization-centred education fits.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Zhu Xi regarded Confucian civilization as superior; extending it as improvement is inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Education in moral loyalty was central via Four Books curriculum; loyalty to nation as symbols is a modern frame; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race-conscious admissions are a modern American dispute that the sources do not touch.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary design is not covered by the opened sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The adaptability of capitalism is a modern economics debate absent from the sources.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The Sinocentric order of cultural influence over neighbours is part of the tradition; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory strategies are not covered by the sources.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Leninist thesis with no counterpart in Neo-Confucian sources.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Ethical norms were meant to apply in all social life, so owners being free to act on any ground is inferred as opposed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights-based constitutional limits are foreign to a duty-based ethical order; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaties are a modern legal question not addressed by the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rulers were the emperor and selection of officials by learning; election of rulers was not envisioned.

minority-veto.rationale: Public-minded gong over private will and harmony under principle conflict with a single dissenter holding a veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Zhu Xi considered removing a tyrant an extraordinary case that could justify disrupting order, and the Great Learning says losing the people loses the kingdom.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not part of the tradition; the emperor with scholar-officials' remonstrance is the model.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Zhu Xi urged love extending beyond family to all things, but animal ethics is not stated.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Same extension of love to all things with accepted ritual sacrifice and eating of animals; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Great Learning calls the ruler the parent of the people who loves what they love, and Neo-Confucians led relief and education locally.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The tradition's ideal links self-cultivation to ordering the state, though Zhu Xi avoided office much of his life and scholars taught outside government.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The critical theory of mass culture is absent from the tradition's sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems and dependency claims are not addressed in the sources.

native-born-offices.rationale: Office reserved for the native-born is not covered; the examinations were open to learned candidates generally.

party-own-road.rationale: Relations among communist parties are not relevant to the sources.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development aid is a modern topic not covered in the sources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Zhu Xi's circle opposed appeasement of the Jurchen, but modern territorial demands are not stated.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous leadership claims are not covered by the sources on Neo-Confucianism.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism as a constitutional value is outside the scope of the tradition.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Twentieth-century totalitarianism comparisons are not addressed by the sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American Civil War historiography is irrelevant to the tradition.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Reverence for ancestors and tradition suggests preserving inherited commemoration; contested-figure case is not discussed.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources do not address public programmes for boys and men.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not discussed in the sources I opened.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Zhu Xi held that the empire needed Confucian ethics to meet challenges from outsiders, supporting distinct civilizational institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Civil moral rule over martial authority is the Confucian ideal.

paid-care-work.rationale: Payment for domestic work is a modern feminist proposal not discussed by the sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Zhu Xi makes filial piety and respect for elder brothers foundational, and Family Rituals specifies ongoing duties to parents including mourning.

office-by-exam.rationale: Zhu Xi's Four Books became the core of the civil-service examinations from about 1314 to 1905, and the school regarded learning-based selection as the proper route.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign ownership of firms is a modern question the sources do not address.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Family Rituals treat marriage as a ritual and lineage bond; easy divorce is inferred as opposed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not addressed in the tradition; inferred from rule by trained officials.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; family support in old age is expected.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure by use is not described in the opened sources, so no position is drawn.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not part of the tradition, as the sources show no such institution.

single-official-language.rationale: Classical written Chinese as common language of the examination system supports one standard language; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign landholding is not discussed in the opened sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not framed in these terms; selection by merit and examination favours individual attainment.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Great Learning ranks virtue above wealth and condemns pursuit of gain, and Neo-Confucians stress restraining excessive desire.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Moral example rather than force; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bloc discipline by military intervention is a Cold War topic outside the tradition.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Great Learning's warning against profit-driven rule suggests criticism of wealth steering government; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding of civil society is a modern question the sources do not address.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Lineage continuity and filial duty to continue the family suggest approval; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local autonomy supported but this specific measure is not addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employer-of-last-resort policy is modern and not discussed by the sources.

democratic-peace.rationale: The democratic peace thesis is a modern theory not found in the sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Ritual, filial piety and principle bind persons to social roles and the order, so no general duty to obey is contrary.

non-intervention.rationale: The sources do not state a view on intervention between states.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is a modern labour issue not addressed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy theory against minorities contradicts universal moral principle and cultivation of all persons.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage as the ritual basis of family and lineage is central to Family Rituals.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom-of-information rights are modern and not addressed in the sources.

local-production.rationale: Local sourcing of goods is not discussed in the opened sources.

informal-organisation.rationale: Voluntary local communities were encouraged, but this tactical question is not addressed.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Precedence of constitutional over international law is a modern matter not in the sources.

religious-nation.rationale: Identity defined by Confucian culture and learning rather than a shared religion; Neo-Confucians opposed Buddhism but did not define the nation by faith.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Sinocentric tribute order with ritual deference to the Middle Kingdom is part of the tradition's background.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Local autonomy supported; revenue questions not addressed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Household property assumed in family order; not stated.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold War anti-communism is anachronistic and the sources give no stance.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Voluntary local organizations providing education and relief alongside government service fits mixed provision.

religion-illusion.rationale: Heaven and ritual are meaningful, though Neo-Confucians criticized Buddhism; religion as illusion is rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: A historical-stage view of capitalism is Marxist and not found in the sources.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not framed in these terms; roles grounded in ritual order.

socialized-care.rationale: Family Rituals and filial piety place care of parents and children within the household.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not covered in the opened sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not addressed in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Voluntary community-centred local organizations focused on education and relief resemble cooperative local communities, though without common property.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settlement policies for ethnic majorities are not discussed in the sources.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The sources do not discuss historical claims to land as against present residents.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Neo-Confucian rational inquiry into the real world gives no basis for denying historical facts.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents split.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Zhu Xi was himself a victim of a factional persecution and the tradition upholds remonstrance.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not a feature of the tradition; Buddhism was refuted by argument.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Rule for the people as parent rather than for revenue; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is an Islamic legal doctrine with no relation to Neo-Confucian sources.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Remonstrance and extraordinary removal only for a tyrant; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Tradition favours guidance by learned moral persons, though local community bodies were voluntary and participatory.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Distinct role-based gender order in ritual; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Filial duty to preserve the body and parents; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The left-right spectrum is a modern frame the sources do not use.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Civilizational culture was defined by acquisition through learning, not exclusion; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Rulers hold Heaven's mandate in the broader Confucian tradition, but Neo-Confucian principle li is impersonal, so the claim fits only loosely.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules are not covered in the sources on the tradition.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment contract rules are modern and not addressed by the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: The sources do not discuss a mixed market economy with social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not Neo-Confucian; inferred from the empire's security concerns.

rich-first.rationale: Differential development order is not covered by the sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Great-power bloc neutrality is not covered by the sources.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Neo-Confucian orthodoxy served hereditary monarchies for centuries, though Mencian teaching allowed a tyrant to lose the mandate.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Zhu Xi's community granary lent grain to farmers at low interest through local voluntary management; inferred, as he did not propose user-owned banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anachronistic; Zhu Xi's benevolent government suggests care for the people but sources give no guide on foreign creditors.

property-franchise.rationale: Officials were to be chosen by learning and virtue rather than wealth, which suggests rejecting a property test; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Neo-Confucianism kept hierarchy between men and women, though it sought harmony with the cosmic principle; the specific claim is inferred as rejected.

reification.rationale: The doctrine treats profit-seeking as the root of disorder but grounds relations in ritual and principle, not in a critique of commodity forms; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Anachronistic; sources say nothing about presses or wealth, and the doctrine's moral concern with the rich points both ways.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule by virtue and ritual was preferred to government by punishments and statutes, so fixed legal codes were not the central safeguard; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Moral cultivation was open to all, so a descent-based franchise conflicts with its principles, though Sinocentrism is present; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic and never discussed; the doctrine's focus on moral rulers and learned officials gives no clear line.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine favours trusted moral officials, and nothing in sources addresses publishing records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Zhu Xi's Family Rituals regulated marriage but sources do not address religious difference; inferred as split.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Moral philosophy that stresses benevolence and harmony; inferred as opposed to deliberate shunning of a group.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Authority was to rest with learned, virtuous officials and the ruler; inferred as opposed to lay selection by lot.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Neo-Confucianism itself recast Confucian teaching against Buddhism, yet it treated the classics as fixed orthodoxy; adherents' stance is split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred: the Great Learning warns against revenue-seeking and says wealth follows virtue, and Neo-Confucians held selfish profit as the root of disorder, so they would favour curbing great fortunes, but not in terms of liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred: the school's ritual and family order centres on lineage, and the sources do not address the question.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: Neo-Confucians criticised Buddhism and Daoism and made moral cultivation the state's task, so teaching unbelief would be opposed; the question is anachronistic.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: the school held that rulers govern by virtue and ritual but kept law and punishment as backstops; no source describes abolishing them.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: Neo-Confucian politics is hierarchical, with rule by virtuous, learned officials selected by examination, not by community shares; unstated.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Neo-Confucians preferred local voluntary institutions of education and relief, such as community granaries and academies, to court centralisation.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: the ideal is long service by virtuous, learned officials and a sage-ruler; limiting terms is a modern device that sources do not address.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: the school's political ideal is rule by moral exemplars chosen by learning, not voter delegation; anachronistic.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Never addressed; a medieval moral philosophy had no view on extinction risk, and its concern for posterity does not settle priority.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: Neo-Confucian ritual and family order is male-led, and the sources do not discuss religious offices.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: Zhu Xi's Family Rituals and the school's filial and hierarchical order give the husband the senior place in the household.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: order rests on family, ritual and local community ties, so political membership by residence alone is unlikely; not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: Local relief and granary institutions show concern for the poor, but rents and price controls are not addressed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Anachronistic: no source addresses intellectual property; adherents would have no common line.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: it preferred voluntary local academies and family ritual to centrally run drilled organisations.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic: nuclear weapons postdate it; its principles do not settle basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on a self-governing moral order; foreign bases are not discussed.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic: the question was not addressed and its moral emphasis points both ways.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Great Learning treats virtue as the root of wealth and warns against revenue-seeking, and Neo-Confucians saw selfish profit as the root of disorder; rent is not specifically discussed.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: Zhu Xi accepted just punishment and, exceptionally, removing a tyrant, so absolute non-violence was not its position.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from its project of restoring and transmitting the ancient Confucian Way as a continuous cultural tradition.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: it grounded gender hierarchy in cosmic principle and ritual; the question was not addressed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: Family Rituals fixed distinct roles for women within the family order.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: ritual and loyalty to the ruler honoured those who died in service, though sainthood for the nation is not its concept.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Its politics is a moral cultivation of rulers and people, not a cosmic struggle; adherents differ on the framing.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: its ideal is a universal moral order, not a nation's diaspora; the question was not addressed.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Great Learning orders the state by first cultivating the person and family, and Neo-Confucians stressed cultural restoration and moral renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Li is an impersonal principle rather than a gendered God, so the question does not map neatly.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: it treated the classics as authoritative and set them as the examination curriculum.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: its universalist moral order was not ethnic, though a Han-centred culture was assumed; not discussed.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: its administration rested on prefectures and officials selected by learning, not peoples; not discussed.

independent-unions.rationale: Not a Song-Ming question; Confucian order rests on hierarchy and loyalty to ruler and family, so independent unions are inferred as foreign to it.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Modern question the school never addressed; its moral hierarchy gives no clear line on workers' power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Zhu Xi favoured local voluntary institutions such as community granaries run for relief, which suggests essentials serving the common good; inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Not discussed; Neo-Confucian government rested on a ruler advised by learned officials and an expert review committee, with no stated bicameralism.

municipal-property.rationale: Local community ownership of production is a modern idea; the school accepted private and family property under moral rule, inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Zhu Xi preferred local voluntary institutions to centralisation but kept the imperial hierarchy, so binding-free confederation is not its model; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Confucian ethics put the family at the centre and the ruler's duty is to make the people prosper, so a wage supporting a household fits its principles.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; the school has no stated position on medical regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; filial piety and care for life suggest sympathy, but no stated position.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The school favoured moral order and virtuous rulers' oversight; untraceable money is inferred as unwelcome.

online-anonymity.rationale: Confucian ethics stress reputation, accountability and the rectification of names; anonymity is inferred as at odds with that.

person-over-state.rationale: The school holds that the individual is embedded in family and ritual order and that private selfishness (si) gives way to public good (gong).

spiritual-nature.rationale: Neo-Confucianism is a spiritual-ethical philosophy of self-cultivation toward sagehood, with politics serving moral education, as the IEP and SEP describe.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Local administration under the imperial centre is the model, and the centre could set limits; inferred, not stated.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, though the school valued agrarian and village life.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The school held that moral order rests on family and ritual, not on universal racial interests; organising by race is inferred as alien to it.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in lineage and ancestors is central to ritual, but race as such is a modern category; inferred, so split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Confucian thought favoured benevolent rule over conquest; warfare is justified mainly for defence or restoration, inferred from this.

missingStatements.text: Rulers should be bound to cultivate their own virtue and set a moral example before they require it of the people.
missingStatements.rationale: The Great Learning, central to the Four Books, says the ruler must himself have the good qualities before requiring them of others, and ties ordering the state to cultivating the person.

missingStatements.text: Anyone, whatever their birth, can become a moral exemplar through sustained study and self-cultivation.
missingStatements.rationale: Zhu Xi held that anyone who sincerely commits to self-cultivation can make real progress toward sagehood, and aimed to open learning to all.
missingStatements.declined: Educational perfectibility is shared by many traditions and does not separate ideologies; not worth a permanent statement.

missingStatements.text: Funeral, wedding and ancestor rites should be observed according to a fixed ritual code.
missingStatements.rationale: Zhu Xi's Family Rituals gave detailed guidance for weddings, funerals and ancestor veneration, and li is described as the social glue that holds society together.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Confucian ritual practice; too niche for the shared bank.

notes: Wang Yangming's school stresses the innate knowing of the mind-heart and would answer statements about authority and expertise somewhat more individualistically. Qing evidential scholars and Chen Liang's pragmatists dissent from Zhu Xi on institutions. Many answers are low-confidence inferences because economic, land and law policies were not covered in the opened sources.
